question: Q1: does a contextual gate beat constant-weight stacking? No mechanistic prior is fitted, so Q2 is not addressed.
prespecification_caveat: these three endpoints were named after the context probe was run on these same donors. A new protocol can govern what happens next; it cannot convert that choice into independent evidence. Every other endpoint is reported as a sensitivity analysis under the same adjustment.

corrects.leak_1_arm_pair_chosen_on_the_whole_coho: the context probe picked the two compared arms from mean losses over every individual before splitting. The pair is now chosen inside each fold from training rows only.
corrects.leak_2_one_cached_prediction_layer: stacking weights were fitted on out-of-fold predictions whose base models had been trained on the very individuals the weights were then scored on. The arms are now refit inside every outer fold.
corrects.overstated_3_probe_verdict_names: an adjusted interval excluding zero was named CONTEXT_CARRIES_SIGNAL even at rho 0.17, below the declared 0.30 margin. The floor now applies to both sides.
corrects.unfixable_4_endpoint_selection: the three endpoints were selected on these data and are labelled accordingly.

positive_control.what_this_proves: the nested harness recovers a contextual gain that is really there, and loses it when the context is permuted. A null X vs K on a real cohort is therefore a statement about that cohort and not about this implementation.

grid_sensitivity.why: the frozen grid hit its own edges often. If X still does not beat K with a grid two octaves wider on each side, the null is not a consequence of the grid.

clinical::linear.how_to_read: A rank correlation near zero and a sign agreement near the share of the majority class mean the context carries no information about which arm will win, so a gate would have nothing to learn. But that is only a REFUTATION when the interval's upper bound falls below the minimum interesting association; otherwise it is a non-detection, and at these cohort sizes it usually is. And an interval that excludes zero while sitting below the floor is a real but TOO SMALL association, which is not the same claim as reaching the declared margin.

And an interval that excludes zero while sitting below the floor is a real but TOO SMALL association, which is not the same claim as reaching the declared margin.

clinical::linear.how_to_read: A rank correlation near zero and a sign agreement near the share of the majority class mean the context carries no information about which arm will win, so a gate would have nothing to learn. But that is only a REFUTATION when the interval's upper bound falls below the minimum interesting association; otherwise it is a non-detection, and at these cohort sizes it usually is. And an interval that excludes zero while sitting below the floor is a real but TOO SMALL association, which is not the same claim as reaching the declared margin.
